rule: A war is on the map if it had organized fighting with roughly a thousand or more deaths in the past twelve months, or is an active war between states, and an outside state fights there or backs a side.
color_rule: Five states get a color: the ones that fight in or back a side in the most wars. Everyone else is grey and labelled.

open.note: The backer says so itself, or the side it helps shows the help in public and the backer does not deny it. A backer's words count as a source only when entered as one. Where the backer denies one kind of help and admits another, the tie is graded on what it admits and the table shows the denial. A tracker that compiles governments' own announcements, such as the Kiel Institute's, counts as their record. Where the backer says something else about what it is doing, the table carries its words beside ours.

shown.note: The evidence is in a public document by a body outside the fight: a UN panel report, a sanctions finding by a state that is not in the war, a weapon recovered and traced. The backer denies it or says nothing.

reported.note: A government outside the fight, named press, a research body or a tracker says so. Nothing has been shown in public. Where one publisher alone carries it, the table says one publisher.

claimed.note: Only a side in the fight says so. No one outside the fight has said so.

kinds.shield: shoots down missiles and drones aimed at it
kinds.cover: backs it in public and at the UN
kinds.harbor: lets its fighters shelter inside its borders

band_note: Deaths are a band for the past twelve months, because the counters disagree. Each entry names who counted. About a thousand is 500 to 1,500; thousands is 1,500 to 10,000; tens of thousands is over 10,000. Where two counters land in different bands, the map draws the lower and the card gives both. A party's own figure is a claim and never sets the band by itself. Where two counts differ by more than two times, the card gives both.
label_note: label: [dx, dy, anchor] offset of the war's name from its glyph, in map units; anchor is start, middle or end

areas_rule: The colored view shades the provinces with ground fighting, sieges, or an air campaign against them in the past twelve months. A province hit only by the occasional long-range drone or missile is not shaded. Provinces are the unit the conflict trackers report, so the shading follows their borders, not front lines.
tier_note: The line answers one question: how do we know? The more broken the line, the less the backer has owned. These words grade the evidence for a line, never a speaker; the Word keeps one verb for everyone.
naming_rule: A state is named as it registers itself at the United Nations, in the short form it uses in English: Türkiye, Myanmar, Czechia, Eswatini. Armed groups keep their common name with their own name beside it.
pressure_rule: A state is also on the map where it uses military force or a blockade against another state, or on its territory, without sustained fighting: strikes, raids, seizures, sinkings. These are drawn as hollow squares with no lines and no death band; who helps whom is on the card. One is entered only when the acting state says so itself.
participants_rule: The participants view shades whole countries by their part: darkest where there is fighting on its own soil, lighter for a state in a war or using force from outside its borders, lightest for a state that backs a side. A country takes its darkest shade. Pick a state and only its wars are shaded: the ones it fights in or backs now. Its own country is outlined. A tie that has ended does not count here; its line still shows, dotted. Pick a war and only that war is shaded. The colored view narrows the same way.
motion_rule: Step back through the year. A war appears in the month its fighting began. A line appears in the month the help began. A line with no start month is older than this year and is there from the first frame, faint. A ring marks a war with something new that month; wars with nothing new that month are dimmed. A heavy line begins that month; a medium line began earlier this year. Lines are drawn as we know them today, not as they were known at the time. Circle size is the year's deaths and does not change with the month. One thing after another is not one thing because of another.
grid_rule: One row per state, one column per war or square. A mark is a tie. The lane says which party it helps; the line says how we know. A filled square means the state fights there itself. A mark is a tie on this map, not a measure of how much. A state with marks in lanes on opposing sides is on both sides. Faint and dated means it switched or stopped. Only states in two or more columns are shown unless you ask for all.

source_classes.backer: the backer itself: its government, armed forces, state media or arms makers
source_classes.recipient: the side the backer helps, speaking for itself
source_classes.opponent: the other side in the fight, or a state that fights there or backs the other side with troops, strikes, bases or air defence; what it finds is a claim
source_classes.document: a public record by a body outside the fight: a UN panel or mission report, a weapon traced, a cargo photographed
source_classes.research: a tracker, institute or rights group
source_classes.reference: an encyclopedia page; it points at the sources but is not one

source_rule: Each tie lists its sources with a class, a date where we have one, and a link where we have one. A source without a link says so. A source that shows the help ending, or something beside the help, is marked and does not date the tie. A reference page never carries a tier by itself; 1 tie still links only a reference page. 1 on-the-record tie rests on a tracker without the backer's own words linked. 3 entries say press reporting without naming the outlet. A documented tie stands on its document; 5 name a UN report without a link. A reported tie wants two sources of different class, or two publishers not relaying the same officials; 5 have one publisher behind them and say so. This is the next work.
finding_rule: A finding by a state that fights in the war, or backs the other side in it, counts as alleged unless the thing found is public: a weapon recovered and traced, a cargo photographed, a document released. A sanctions notice names firms; it does not show the evidence. Press that only relays a party's officials counts as that party. A press item names whom it cites; where it only relays one side's officials, it is that side.
evidence_rule: Every tie carries the date of its latest dated source that shows the help. A source that shows the help ending, or reversing, ends the tie or leaves its date where it was; it does not refresh it. A tie whose sources all come from before the window, or carry no date, is drawn faint and the table says so. A bare year that is the window's own year counts as inside it.

ucdp_note: UCDP counts deaths in fighting, deaths in fighting between armed groups, and civilians killed on purpose, each with a low, best and high. UCDP calls a conflict a war at a thousand battle deaths in a year and minor below that. The figures here are our own sums from data/ucdp.json, built by scripts/build_ucdp.py from the yearly file and the monthly candidate files, pulled after the 20th of each month. A few UCDP rows carry a high below their best; we sum them as given. A flag is UCDP's own mark that a row still needs a check on its deaths, its sides, its place or its source.
tie_form: A tie is one line from a backer to a side: who helps, whom, with what (the kinds), how we know (the tier), what the backer says about it (the stance), since when and how exact that date is, when it ended if it did, the sources by class with dates and links, the date of the latest dated source, the date the row was entered, and the date a person last checked it. The data is one file, data/conflicts.json, and this page draws it.
